content.user_title: Build Azure Event Hubs Rust Clients
content.value_statement: Rust teams need concise guidance for Azure Event Hubs producers, consumers, batches, and partitions. This skill provides focused SDK examples for common streaming ingestion tasks.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to add Azure Event Hubs Rust SDK dependencies.
Documents environment variables for the Event Hubs namespace and hub name.
Provides producer setup examples with DeveloperToolsCredential.
Shows single event and batch sending patterns.
Provides consumer, partition receiver, and metadata lookup examples.
Mentions optional blob checkpoint store support for distributed consumers.
limitations: It does not validate Azure credentials or provision cloud resources.
It does not include a complete production application.
It does not cover every Event Hubs configuration option.
Users must test examples against their own Azure environment.

use_cases.title: Prototype Streaming Producers
use_cases.description: Create a small Rust producer that sends events or batches to Azure Event Hubs.

use_cases.title: Build Consumer Workflows
use_cases.description: Use partition receivers to read events and inspect Event Hub metadata.

use_cases.title: Plan Distributed Consumption
use_cases.description: Identify when checkpointing and consumer groups are needed for parallel processing.

prompt_templates.title: Add Event Hubs Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add the Rust crates needed for Azure Event Hubs and explain what each crate does.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Producer
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating an Azure Event Hubs producer client in Rust with DeveloperToolsCredential.

prompt_templates.title: Send Events in Batches
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to send batched event data to Azure Event Hubs in Rust and explain capacity checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Partition Consumer
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Rust consumer that reads from Event Hub partitions and plans for checkpointing.

output_examples.input: I need to send telemetry from a Rust service to Azure Event Hubs.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline dependency setup, credential selection, producer client creation, and when to send single events or batches.

output_examples.input: I want to read events from one Event Hub partition.
output_examples.output: The skill would describe creating a consumer client, opening a partition receiver, receiving events, and reviewing partition metadata.

output_examples.input: My service needs parallel consumers with progress tracking.
output_examples.output: The skill would explain consumer groups, independent partition processing, and optional checkpoint store support.

best_practices: Reuse Event Hubs clients instead of creating new clients for each event.
Use batches for efficient ingestion when event size and capacity allow it.
Use consumer groups and checkpointing for distributed consumers.
anti_patterns: Do not treat sample placeholders as production configuration.
Do not skip error handling around sends, receives, and batch capacity checks.
Do not run consumers without a checkpointing plan when progress must be durable.

faq.question: Does this skill provision Azure Event Hubs resources?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Rust SDK usage after the Azure resources already exist.

faq.question: Which Rust crate does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on azure_messaging_eventhubs and related Azure identity and checkpoint store crates.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: It shows DeveloperToolsCredential in examples, but users must select credentials for their environment.

faq.question: Can it help with batched sending?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes the create batch flow and the need to check batch capacity.

faq.question: Can it help with receiving events?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes consumer creation, partition receivers, and metadata lookup examples.

faq.question: Is it safe to use as production guidance?
faq.answer: Use it as a starting point. Production systems need testing, monitoring, retries, and environment-specific validation.
